verdict.rationale: First-party docs describe the whole issue-to-PR flow: it reads issues from GitHub/GitLab, writes code, runs tests, and submits PRs. The MCP docs give the concrete example "Add the feature described in JIRA issue ENG-4521 and create a PR on GitHub," and Slack bug reports can also come back as pull requests. Community complaints about output quality and self-verification are general, not concrete failures of this workflow. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of the end-to-end issue-to-PR flow, and docs on non-GitHub trackers beyond needing MCP server setup (e.g., Jira).

support.subject: As a developer, I can turn a tracked issue into a complete pull request end-to-end

citations.quote: Claude Code integrates with GitHub, GitLab, and your command line tools to handle the entire workflow—reading issues, writing code, running tests, and submitting PRs—all from your terminal.
Implement features from issue trackers: "Add the feature described in JIRA issue ENG-4521 and create a PR on GitHub."
It stages changes, writes commit messages, creates branches, and opens pull requests.
mention @Claude in Slack with a bug report and get a pull request back
